idea: Financial modelling course for architects and developers
pain: They cannot model a development and it costs them work and money
v1: A six-module course with working templates
channel: Her architecture network plus professional bodies
verdict: Uniquely well-placed to teach this, sold to a warm audience - but a small and poor one.

why.distribution: Her architecture network plus professional bodies gives a real warm route to this audience.
why.demand: Architects do pay for CPD, though typically modest amounts.
why.fmf: An architect who became an equity analyst is the only credible person to teach this.
why.revenue_structure: One-off course purchases; each student buys once.
why.defensibility: The dual credibility is the moat and it is genuine.
why.ceiling: £900 x 220 students = £198k, requiring a fifth of the UK's small-practice architects.

ceiling_arithmetic: £900 x 220 students = £198k. That implies reaching a substantial share of UK architects willing to spend £900 on CPD. Realistic: 60-100 = £54-90k, which is a genuinely decent outcome for a recorded product.
carries: A monopoly on credibility for this specific course, sold into a warm and identifiable audience with CPD budgets.
kills: One-off revenue and a finite audience - once the profession has bought it, growth stops.
test: Pre-sell at £700 to twenty architects before recording anything.
